note: Landmark spots (#216). Design: design/gdd/landmark-discovery.md. `at` and every zone are [x, z] in level meters. `find.edge` is the distance to the footprint, and `find.reach` (a large spot, a park) keeps that zone within that many meters of `at`; `find.r` is a circle at `find.at` (or `at`). Each fact has a primary source; the quote behind each fact is in docs/research/2026-11-10-landmark-facts.md. Check a change with `npm run validate:landmarks`.

spots.name: Ponce City Market
spots.short: Opened in 1926 as a nine-story Sears, Roebuck and Co. store and warehouse.

card.text: The Sears, Roebuck and Co. building opened to customers in 1926, nine stories of reinforced concrete and brick.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Atlantans flocked to the opening of the Sears retail store on August 2, 1926.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Its central tower facing Ponce de Leon Avenue carries Italian Renaissance Revival ornament.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Nimmons & Company designed it, along with Sears' other distribution centers of the mid-1920s.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Shops, the Central Food Hall and BeltLine access opened at Ponce City Market in 2015.

challenge.hint: Land a 2,000 point combo on the trail

spots.name: Ford Factory Lofts
spots.short: Ford built Model T's here from 1915 in a plant with rail cars rolling inside.

card.text: The Ford Motor Company Assembly Plant was built in 1914-15, four stories of reinforced concrete.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Model T's (1915-1927), Model A's (1927-1932) and V-8's (1932-1937) were assembled here.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: The building was headquarters of Ford's Southeastern operations from 1915 to 1942.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: A reinforced second floor carried a railbed, so rail cars rolled into the building to unload.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: It is one of three surviving early Ford assembly plants in the South, with Houston and Dallas.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

challenge.hint: Grind the Ponce curb for 9 m

spots.name: New Realm Brewing
spots.short: A favorite on the Eastside Trail since 2018, with a rooftop view of the city.

card.text: New Realm Brewing Company has been a favorite along the Eastside Trail since 2018.
Its rooftop looks out over the city and one of the busiest parts of the BeltLine corridor.
New Realm makes its own beer and spirits and hosts trivia, vintage market pop-ups and live music.

challenge.hint: Land a 600 point combo on the trail

spots.name: Telephone Factory Lofts
spots.short: Built 1939-1941 for Western Electric, maker of Bell telephones.

card.text: The Western Electric Company Building was constructed from 1939 to 1941.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Western Electric's in-house architect Walter R. Kattelle designed it in the Streamline Moderne style.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Western Electric built it for warehousing, repair and light manufacturing.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: The original plans show classrooms, so the building trained employees as well as housing their work.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Today each floor of the old manufacturing and office section holds 18 loft apartments.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

challenge.hint: Ride the 3 rings in order in 14 s

spots.name: Krog Street Market
spots.short: A dining hall and shops on the former Atlanta Stove Works factory site.

card.text: Krog Street Market stands on the former Atlanta Stove Works factory site.
Krog Street Market is in Inman Park, right along the BeltLine Eastside Trail.
It has a communal dining hall and shops you can reach on foot, by bike, or by car.

challenge.hint: Grind the Krog Street curb for 15 m

spots.name: Studioplex
spots.short: A 1905 cotton warehouse on Auburn Avenue, now loft apartments.

card.text: The Atlantic Compress Company built the large cotton warehouse and platform in 1905.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: From the early 1920s until 1944 the Southeastern Compress and Warehouse Company ran the facility.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Southeastern ran eighteen warehouses and could store 750,000 bales of cotton at one time.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: A 100,000-gallon concrete water tower, built in 1907, stands northwest of the warehouse.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: A certified rehabilitation converted the cotton warehouse to loft apartments.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

challenge.hint: Hop on the Auburn Avenue sidewalk

spots.name: Ponce de Leon Avenue Bridge
spots.short: A ramp joins Ponce de Leon Avenue to the trail at the bridge by Ponce City Market.

card.text: Ponce streetscape work includes a ramp to the Eastside Trail at the northwest corner of the Ponce de Leon Avenue bridge.
The final stage of the Ponce de Leon Avenue ramp to the Eastside Trail was completed in November 2025.
The Eastside Trail was the first finished section of the Atlanta BeltLine in the old rail corridor.

challenge.hint: Hop on the bridge over Ponce

spots.name: North Avenue Bridge
spots.short: North Avenue Bridge crosses the street with the Atlanta skyline behind it.

card.text: North Avenue Bridge on the Eastside Trail crosses the street with the skyline in the background.
The North Avenue bridge connects the Old Fourth Ward and Poncey-Highland neighborhoods.
With traffic below and buildings above, the North Avenue Bridge is a favorite place for photos.
The giant puppet Little Amal's Eastside Trail walk was planned with a stop on the North Avenue Bridge.

challenge.hint: Ride the 3 rings in order in 14 s

spots.name: Ralph McGill Boulevard Bridge
spots.short: A tower for chimney swifts stands on the trail just north of Ralph McGill Blvd.

card.text: In April 2021 a chimney swift tower was installed on the Eastside Trail north of Ralph McGill Blvd.
Georgia Audubon and Atlanta BeltLine, Inc. partnered on the towers to support chimney swift birds.
The trail link to Historic Fourth Ward Park is the first phase of the development at 760 Ralph McGill Boulevard.
New stairs and an elevator reconnecting the trail and Historic Fourth Ward Park opened in April 2021.

challenge.hint: Grind the curb below the bridge for 15 m

spots.name: Freedom Parkway Bridge
spots.short: A BeltLine Marketplace sits under the John Lewis Freedom Parkway Bridge.

card.text: A BeltLine Marketplace sits underneath the John Lewis Freedom Parkway Bridge on the Eastside Trail.
The skatepark sits alongside the BeltLine corridor in the shadow of Freedom Parkway.
The Atlanta BeltLine is easily reached from Freedom Park's trail network.

challenge.hint: Hop under the Freedom Parkway bridge

spots.name: Historic Fourth Ward Park
spots.short: The park's lake doubles as a stormwater basin; the park opened in 2011.

card.text: Historic Fourth Ward Park opened in 2011.
The centerpiece of the park is a lake that doubles as a stormwater retention basin.
The lake's permanent pool comes from natural groundwater.
Residents, businesses, the city's watershed department and Atlanta BeltLine, Inc. designed the park together.
The Historic Fourth Ward Park Conservancy was formed in 2008 as the park's non-profit support arm.

challenge.hint: Land a 1,000 point combo by the pond

spots.name: Freedom Park
spots.short: Freedom Park links 7 neighborhoods with 8 miles of paths on 130+ acres.

card.text: Freedom Park has 130+ acres and 8 miles of paths for walking, jogging, and cycling.
Freedom Park links 7 neighborhoods, including Inman Park, Old Fourth Ward, and Poncey-Highland.
Since 2007 the city of Atlanta has designated Freedom Park as Atlanta's Art Park.
Freedom Park is the only park in the world that includes two Nobel Peace Centers.
Freedom Park is Atlanta's largest linear park.

challenge.hint: Ride the 3 rings in order in 24 s

spots.name: Thomas Taylor Memorial Skatepark
spots.short: Atlanta's first public skatepark, open since spring 2011.

card.text: It is Atlanta's first public skatepark, designed with input from the local skateboard community.
The skatepark opened in spring 2011.
Tony Hawk appeared at the grand opening, and his foundation gave $25,000 toward construction.
The skatepark was renamed in 2024 to honor Thomas F. Taylor, a skateboarder and advocate for Atlanta skating.
Solar panels offset roughly 50 percent of the park's energy costs.

challenge.hint: Land a 2,000 point combo in the skatepark

spots.name: Inman Park Historic District
spots.short: Atlanta's first planned suburb, laid out from 1889 by Joel Hurt.

card.text: Inman Park was the first planned residential suburb developed in Atlanta.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Developer Joel Hurt laid out the roughly 135-acre neighborhood from 1889 to 1891.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Inman Park featured one of the nation's first electric streetcar lines, along Edgewood Avenue.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: Coca-Cola founder Asa Candler and hardware founder George E. King built homes in Inman Park.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

card.text: The Inman Park Historic District was listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.

source.name: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

spots.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum
spots.short: Dedicated October 1, 1986; home to a life-size replica of the Oval Office.

card.text: The Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum was dedicated on October 1, 1986.

source.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum

card.text: Ground was broken on October 2, 1984; donations from friends around the world raised $26 million.

source.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum

card.text: Japanese master gardener Kinsaku Nakane designed its Japanese Garden.

source.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum

card.text: The library houses 40,000,000 pages, 1,000,000 photographs and 2,500 hours of video.

source.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum

card.text: The museum has a life-size replica of the Oval Office and a Camp David cabin-style exhibit.

source.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum
